connections.why: Forces are what change an object's motion through Newton's laws
Work done by a force is the energy transferred to or from a store
Kinetic theory explains internal energy, heating and changes of state
Nuclear fission and fusion are major sources of energy
Electrical power is one of the most important energy transfers
The motor effect produces a force on a current in a magnetic field
Moving charge creates magnetic effects, linking circuits to motors and generators
Light is a wave, so reflection and refraction follow general wave behaviour
Red shift in light from galaxies is evidence for an expanding universe
Nuclear fusion is the energy source that powers stars
Orbital motion applies the ideas of speed, force and gravity to planets
Motion and force are investigated through quantitative practical work
Circuit experiments require careful measurement and data-handling skills
Optics practicals develop measurement, ray-tracing and analysis skills
Density and gas-law experiments build core practical technique
